items.title: Quadratic-question nonlocal games robustly forcing Pauli measurements
items.difficulty_reason: The authors construct a synchronous nonlocal game from spectral-gap measures, derive a quantitative twisted commutation relation from near-perfect play, round it using the finite-group stability theorem, and identify the resulting Weyl–Heisenberg representation with Pauli measurements. The quadratic question count uses the explicitly cited small-support spectral-gap/code result. The source-local construction and stability proof are retained in full, not hidden as background; the cited external code result is attributed.

Author game definitions, Pauli measurements, game construction and near-optimal strategy argument

readability.basis: Reused original publisher 29-page PDF in the fixed work. Physically viewed pages 21–23, including game construction estimate, corollary and Theorem 3.11; the full source and reader remain accessible.

dedup.scope: Current master title searches for nonlocal game, non-local game and Pauli, and exact author work inspected. Nearby selected source statement 187312 was read.

compared.relation: Same fixed work; selected Theorem 0.1 concerns stability of direct products of groups with property (T). Theorem 3.11 constructs specific nonlocal games and bounds how near-perfect synchronous strategies approximate Pauli measurements.

Its selected theorem assumes commuting embeddings of measurement algebras for several games with perfect strategies and constructs parallel perfect play; it does not assert robust Pauli self-testing for the constructed quadratic-question family.

source_disclosures: The theorem concerns synchronous strategies and O(epsilon)-closeness in the authors’ specified notion. The source explicitly credits the small-support finite-group spectral-gap result and discusses relation to earlier Pauli tests.
